steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Imamate is a Shi'a Muslim belief that Allah appointed twelve Imams to lead the Muslim community after Muhammad's death. These Imams are divinely chosen, infallible and have special spiritual authority. This is one of the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: The Imamate is the key difference between Sunni and Shi'a Islam. Sunni Muslims believe caliphs should be chosen by the community; Shi'a Muslims believe Allah appointed the Imams. This is why the two traditions have different approaches to authority, law and leadership.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — The Imamate
steps.body: 1. For The Imamate questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Imamate to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In the UK, Shi’a communities follow the guidance of marja (religious authorities) who are considered the most learned scholars qualified to interpret the teachings of the Imams. The Al-Khoei Foundation in London follows the marja’iyya of Ayatollah Sistani, one of the most senior Shi’a clerics in the world.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
